summary: The macOS/Darwin WebRTC texture renderer emitted didFirstFrameRendered on every incoming frame even when no pixel buffer had been uploaded to Flutter's texture. The event now fires only after a buffer is copied and textureFrameAvailable is notified. This makes Flutter's web-parity loading state and first-frame diagnostics more truthful; it does not establish that the reported black Mac stream is fixed.

checks.name: Regression test before fix
checks.observation: The new ordering assertion failed because the renderer had no uploaded-frame gate before emitting didFirstFrameRendered. Existing disposal and shared-source tests passed.

checks.name: Focused macOS renderer lifecycle tests
checks.observation: All 3 tests pass, including upload-before-first-frame ordering, disposal safety, and byte-for-byte parity between common Darwin and macOS renderer implementations.

checks.name: macOS Debug build
checks.observation: Xcode compiled the changed Objective-C renderer and produced build/macos/Build/Products/Debug/BOOHTACORD.app.

limitations: The source-order regression test proves the event is gated by the texture upload path, not that a live Mac compositor displays the pixels.
No active Pixel MediaProjection was present in the latest read-only snapshot, so paired sender/receiver counters were unavailable.
remaining: Retest a still-active Pixel publication on Mac and browser. Confirm the Mac first-frame state clears only when a texture frame is uploaded, compare receiver decoded FPS/framesRendered, and verify unpublish/reselection. Keep FE-61 open until live acceptance passes.
